The search yields the costs 10, 8, 6 and 4 as it finds cheaper edit paths, and ends at 2, the exact distance: insert node B and edge E–B." width="100%"} The exact search behind `graph_edit_distance(exact=True)` finds complete edit paths of strictly decreasing cost until no cheaper one exists. This method yields each of those costs in turn, so the last value is the exact graph edit distance and every earlier one is an upper bound on it. Use it to: - stop early with a good-enough distance, by breaking out of the loop - follow how quickly the search converges on a pair of graphs The whole search runs before the first value is yielded, so breaking out early saves no time; pass `upper_bound=` to `graph_edit_distance()`, or `timeout=` to it or to `optimize_edit_paths()`, to cap the work instead. Parameters are as in `optimal_edit_paths()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [other]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The target graph. It must have the same directedness as the calling graph. Only costs up to this value are yielded. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Iterator[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The costs of successively cheaper edit paths, ending with the edit distance. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graphs differ in directedness, or a cost is negative or not a number. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~graph_edit_distance`) : The final value directly. [](`~optimize_edit_paths`) : The same search, yielding the edit paths too. ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Matches NetworkX's `optimize_graph_edit_distance()` in its final value. The intermediate values depend on the order in which equally good assignments are explored, so they can differ from NetworkX's. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The estimates for a six-node cycle and a seven-node wheel end at the exact distance, `7.0`: ::: {#fdbc06ea .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec cycle = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(6) wheel = ec.Graph().add_wheel_graph(7) list(cycle.optimize_graph_edit_distance(wheel)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [7.0] ``` ::: :::
